changes.comment: BREAKING (implementers only): IAiProviderDescriptor.chatOutputTokensField ('max_tokens' | 'max_completion_tokens', exported type ChatOutputTokensField) now declares the Chat Completions output-token field, and usesMaxCompletionTokensField reads it instead of matching the provider id 'openai' — a hand-built descriptor that relied on id 'openai' to send max_completion_tokens must now declare the field. ai-assist: (1) OpenAI, Groq and xAI Grok declare 'max_completion_tokens' (each API reference marks max_tokens deprecated), so Groq and xAI chat requests now send maxTokens as max_completion_tokens rather than max_tokens; Mistral, Ollama and openai-compat keep max_tokens. Open question: xAI documents max_completion_tokens as bounding visible output only, not reasoning tokens, so a small maxTokens on a reasoning Grok model may cap less than the deprecated max_tokens did. (2) executeClientToolTurn now runs the thinking/temperature conflict check, as the completion and streaming paths do: a temperature beside a caller-built non-'none' effort is refused (e.g. on gpt-6-luna and gpt-6-sol, 1 included) instead of being dropped silently by the OpenAI Responses adapter; that adapter now sends any temperature the caller provided, so on a provider with no thinking discriminator (Groq, Mistral, Ollama, openai-compat) a caller-built effort and temperature are both sent as built. (3) executeClientToolTurn refuses a caller-built OpenAI-format effort 'none' (openAiEffort or xaiEffort) on a model in thinkingRequiredModelPrefixes (gpt-6.1-sol, gpt-6-astra, grok-4.7/4.6/4.5) before the wire; the existing anthropicThinkingDisabled refusal now applies only to Anthropic-format descriptors, the only adapter that reads that flag. (4) resolveProviderModel — and the completion, streaming, client-tool and resolveMaxOutputTokens paths through it — fails with the provider id and the offending key's path on a ModelSpec outside its type (e.g. { base: undefined } from untyped JSON) instead of throwing a TypeError; resolveModel resolves such a spec to ''. Both consult only a spec's own keys, so a context named like an Object.prototype member (e.g. 'constructor') falls back to base. resolveModel and MODEL_SPEC_BASE_KEY are unchanged in the public API (now declared in modelSpecResolver.ts).
